integrations.purpose: Register a correspondence, mint its reference, issue one upload ticket per declared attachment.
Redeem one single-use ticket with the raw file.
Raise a helpdesk case. Never enters the registry.
Mail a one-time code to an address.
Exchange a code for a single-use proof.
Read one submission back, in the public projection only.
A verified citizen responds, adds a note, or withdraws. Appends to the timeline; only withdrawal changes status.
A fixed 60-minute window counter per endpoint per source. Read, then update or create, before the work.
One row per run, written inside the capture scope and never on the request path.
Mint a unique, monotonic reference per year. Replaces the last-three-digits-of-ticks scheme, which yields 1000 values a year and collides.
A receipt that a message was sent. Never the message body, and never a one-time code.

statuses.name: acknowledged
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than in_progress, blocked, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of in_progress, blocked.

statuses.name: action_complete
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from in_progress, awaiting_response through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than pending_review, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of pending_review.
statuses.entryGate: Response evidence is required: a response, a summary or a task id.

statuses.name: approved
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from pending_review, escalated through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_pending, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_pending.

statuses.name: approved_with_edit
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_pending, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_pending.

statuses.name: archived
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than reopen_requested, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of reopen_requested.

statuses.name: arrival
statuses.entryCondition: Not the target of any declared transition: this state can only be an origin.
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than registered, duplicate, rejected, on_hold, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of registered, duplicate, rejected, on_hold.

statuses.name: assigned
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from triage_complete, assigning through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than acknowledged, in_progress, reassign_requested, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of acknowledged, in_progress, reassign_requested.

statuses.name: assigning
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from triage_complete, assignment_failed through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than assigned, assignment_failed, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of assigned, assignment_failed.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to assignment_failed: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: assignment_failed
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than assigning, triage_complete, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of assigning, triage_complete.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to assigning: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: awaiting_response
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than in_progress, action_complete, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of in_progress, action_complete.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to in_progress: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: blocked
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from acknowledged, in_progress through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than in_progress, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of in_progress.
statuses.reversalConditions: Reversible to in_progress: the map declares edges in both directions.

statuses.name: closed
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than archived, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of archived.
statuses.entryGate: The closure gate must pass, through the caller-supplied canClose() helper.

statuses.name: closure_check
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from no_dispatch, dispatched through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than closed, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of closed.

statuses.name: dispatch_failed
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_pending, no_dispatch, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_pending, no_dispatch.

statuses.name: dispatch_in_flight
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatched, dispatch_failed, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatched, dispatch_failed.

statuses.name: dispatch_pending
statuses.entryCondition: Reached from approved, approved_with_edit, dispatch_failed through canTransition().
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than dispatch_in_flight, no_dispatch, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of dispatch_in_flight, no_dispatch.

statuses.name: dispatched
statuses.restrictedActions: Any transition to a state other than closure_check, which canTransition() refuses.
statuses.exitCondition: A caller requests a transition to one of closure_check.

transitions.evidenceNote: Declared edge of the internal-to-public status map.
The mapping is declared, and its own source records this particular edge as a reading rather than a fact, flagged for agency confirmation.
transitions.conflictingReading: "Accepted" means the registry accepted the item for handling, which is the public "Under review". If it instead means the request itself was granted, it maps to "approved".
transitions.conflictAuthorityAssessment: Both readings come from the same artifact, so neither is more current than the other and neither can settle the question. The artifact is authoritative for what the software DOES — it is the map the renderer calls — and is explicitly not authoritative for what the status MEANS to the agency, which it defers.
transitions.conflictImplementationRelevance: Implemented: the declared edge is what governedStatusLabel() returns today. A citizen is already being shown 'review' for a record the platform holds as 'Accepted'.
transitions.conflictValidationRequired: The registry owner states which reading is intended. If the alternative is intended, the map changes and, for the archived case, a distinct public state is needed.
transitions.validationStatus: Requires confirmation by the named owner

controls.name: Acknowledgement receipt
controls.description: Receipt of an assignment is confirmed and recorded before work starts.
controls.condition: The payload carries every required field, including an idempotency key.
controls.expectedBehaviour: A receipt is written to the ledger with actor, time, source and the idempotency key.
controls.outcome: A duplicate acknowledgement inside the dedupe window is recognised as the same receipt, not a second one.
controls.exception: A failed send is retried under the declared retry policy and queued when it cannot be delivered.
controls.idempotency: An idempotency key is required on every payload.
controls.evidenceNote: Enforcement, retry policy, dedupe window and receipt fields are all declared in configuration.

gaps.subject: Two artifacts authorise a governed action, and only one of them says what the action does
gaps.missingInformation: A per-action governance record for every name the runtime will accept, and a stated precedence between the two authorities.
gaps.availableEvidence: core/action-authority.js accepts an action when the per-action table carries a spec for it OR the module boundary charter lists it in owns[]. The table carries 61 specs, each naming an owner, a service, an audit vocabulary and a backend requirement. The charter declares 132 capability names across 31 modules, of which 90 have no per-action spec. The charter list mixes writes with view capabilities, so its entries cannot be read as actions without checking each one.
gaps.reasonRequired: An action authorised only by the charter runs with no declared service, no declared audit vocabulary and no declared backend requirement, while an action in the table runs with all four. Nothing states which authority governs when they disagree.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: Governed writes exist that this documentation can name but cannot describe: the FastTrack escalation and owner-notification actions are authorised by the charter alone and carry no audit vocabulary of their own.
gaps.operationalRisk: A write reaches the system of record without the audit event a reader of the governance table would expect it to write.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The platform technical owner, as the owner of both configurations.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Every name the runtime will accept as an action has a per-action record, or the charter states explicitly which of its entries are actions and which are views.

gaps.subject: Some governed writes cannot be named from their call site
gaps.missingInformation: The action name at the call site, for the modules that pass it as a variable.
gaps.availableEvidence: 4 module(s) — activities, executive, fasttrack, user-admin — call executeOwnedAction() with the action passed as a variable. Their actions are recovered from the per-action table and, where the name also appears as a literal in the module, from the boundary charter. Every recovered step is classified Inferred and says which recovery produced it.
gaps.reasonRequired: A step recovered by reading two artifacts together is weaker evidence than one read from a single call site, and the difference should not be invisible to a reader.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: For these modules, the mapping from a control the operator presses to the action it raises is a reading rather than a fact.
gaps.operationalRisk: An action could be raised that no artifact declares, and this documentation would not show it.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The module source, if the call sites are changed to name their actions literally.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Each call site names its action literally, or the module declares the set of names it dispatches.

gaps.subject: Nothing fires an escalation when a service-level clock expires

Every action in every supplied export and paste package was walked and catalogued step by step. Business purpose, owner and criticality are unevidenced across the whole estate, so no automated process reaches full documentation from confirmed evidence.
Run records establish that the endpoints execute and what status each returns. They do not establish that any business transaction completed: none of the captured runs carries one.

Entry conditions, exit conditions, permitted actions and audit behaviour are not evidenced for any of them, and no guard governs movement between them. A further 10 module(s) carry a single one of these values; a lone common word does not establish which status set it belongs to, and those are not counted as users.

The cascade mechanism is fully documented: it derives responsible unit, assignee, priority and both clocks from the category. The matrix it applies is not. The 0 rows catalogued are the declared fallback; the live matrix is expected from reference data that is not among the supplied inputs.
20 aliases are declared. The workflow behind each is only partly established, and by design the registry carries no URL.

4 artifact(s) reviewed and found to carry vocabulary, scales or budgets rather than process behaviour: config/priority.config.js, config/receipt-ledger.config.js, config/browser-certification.config.js, config/performance-budget.config.js. Recorded so the review is accountable for them.

25 workspaces declared, each matched to a module file. Their governed writes are catalogued step by step; the rendering, filtering and paging between writes is presentation and is not modelled as process.
61 actions, each with a declared owner, service, audit vocabulary and backend requirement.
6 roles and 4 personas, each with its route set. Server-side authorisation of the caller is not evidenced and is raised as a gap.

265 notification points identified: outbound mail sends in the flow estate and operator-facing outcome messages in the modules. No escalation bound to a service-level clock is evidenced anywhere in the supplied inputs.

106 test files are present and were reviewed. They establish invariants over the implementation — contracts, vocabularies, wiring, encoding, secrets. They do NOT state, per process, what that process is required to do to be accepted, so no process draws its completion criteria from them.

terminology.definition: One node of a workflow definition. Every action names the actions it runs after and the status each must have reached.
A workspace that may raise a governed action it does not own. Ownership, service and audit vocabulary stay with the owner.
The routing matrix that derives responsible unit, assignee, priority and both service-level clocks from a correspondence category.
A scope whose run-after condition admits Failed, TimedOut or Skipped, so it runs when the scope before it did not succeed.
Departmental or service unit. The key by which the routing matrix names a responsible unit.
The name a module uses to reach a workflow. The URL behind it is supplied at runtime and never held in source.
A write that passes through executeOwnedAction(), which refuses it unless the calling module owns it or is a declared allowed invoker.
A workspace not on the sidebar, reached only from a named parent workspace.
One of the values in the frozen internal transition map. Distinct from the public status vocabulary.
One of the seven governed values a citizen is shown. Distinct from the internal lifecycle state.
The condition under which a Power Automate action runs, expressed as the predecessor actions and the statuses each must have reached.
A captured execution of a workflow: its outcome and the response it returned. Evidence of execution, not of business success.
A primary route on the sidebar, implemented by a module of the same name.

evidenceFramework.name: Confirmed
evidenceFramework.definition: A supplied artifact states this directly. Reading that artifact is sufficient to establish it.

evidenceFramework.name: Inferred
evidenceFramework.definition: Derived by reasoning across two or more artifacts. No single artifact states it.

evidenceFramework.name: Partially evidenced
evidenceFramework.definition: Some attributes are stated by an artifact and others are not. The record says which is which.

evidenceFramework.name: Conflicting
evidenceFramework.definition: Two artifacts disagree. Both readings are recorded; neither is silently preferred.

evidenceFramework.name: Unavailable
evidenceFramework.definition: The information is required by this standard and no supplied artifact carries it.

evidenceFramework.name: Not verifiable from the supplied inputs
evidenceFramework.definition: The artifact exists but does not permit the statement to be checked from the supplied inputs alone.

evidenceFramework.name: Requires authoritative validation
evidenceFramework.definition: Readable from an artifact, but the artifact is not authoritative for it. A named owner must confirm.
